results.evidence: Still unsettled. The row's overview, pro_tips, totalNote and partner fields say ~18 pitches / 3,000 ft (the Upper ridge from the notch above the Stuart Glacier), while pitches=20 matches one listing of the Direct/Complete ridge. New search summaries give yet other counts for the Complete ridge (a club route page and a trip-report blog describe the lower half as adding many pitches, one summary says 16 more, another quotes 15 in total); most parties simul-climb the lower ridge, so pitch counts are not a stable published figure and no two independent sources agree on one number.

results.fact: Trailhead pin vs the approach the waypoints and itinerary describe
results.evidence: Unchanged: waypoint 0 is the Stuart Lake Trailhead (north side) and is pinned there, while waypoints 1-2 are Longs Pass and Goat Pass on the south (Esmeralda) approach. Both approaches are genuine for this route, but reconciling the list means choosing one approach and moving or renaming pins, which is out of scope (pin positions). No text patch can fix it without contradicting the map.

results.fact: Bergschrund/glacier hazard on a rock-route approach that has no glacier
results.evidence: Retry: the Gorillas in the Mist route page says the wall 'rises up from the snow' and the first pitch is reached by scrambling, with no bergschrund or moat named; the first-ascent report calls the wall a buttress over the glacier, and a search summary of an approach description mentions only short snowfields under 25 degrees below the Stuart Glacier. No source confirms or rules out a moat/bergschrund at the base, so the watch_out line cannot be removed or confirmed from two sources.

New evidence: a 2020 trip report of the Sherpa Glacier from the Stuart Lake trailhead sits under a hike listing of 11.1 mi round trip / 6,309 ft, and a previously found logged ascent was 11.8 mi round trip; both are far from partner_requirements' '~27 mi' and dist_km 21.73 km (13.5 mi shown as one way). But the 11.1 figure is a generic 'Mount Stuart' hike listing that does not name its approach, the two figures do not match exactly, one other multi-day report gives 25 mi, and no source states a one-way figure for dist_km. Left open rather than write a derived value.

The live row's crux pitch note now says the step 'often holds around 100 ft of water ice up to 60 degrees, with sections described as near 80 degrees' and that it varies from firm snow to verglas, so the prose presents both figures as condition-dependent; max_angle 80 (the upper figure) does not render on the route page.

Three independent sources grade the West Ridge Grade III: the route database page (Grade III, 5.6), a club trip listing ('Grade III, low 5th, extensive 4th class scrambling'), and a detailed personal trip report (III). One peak overview gives II 5.4, but the weight of independent sources and the row's own grade field ('III, 5.4-5.6') agree on III, so commitment and alpine_grade are brought to III.

Still unsettled. One report gives roughly 15-17 mi round trip (near the itinerary's 16.5 mi); a club listing gives 13.0 mi total over three days camp-to-camp with a 5-mile summit day. dist_km 32.2 km (20 mi shown as one way) matches neither, but no source states a one-way approach figure and the round-trip figures disagree, so no patch.

Unchanged on retry: the route database lists 5.12a with the final pitch 5.12- (rock_grade), while the first-ascent party's blog and its journal note give 5.11d / IV 5.11+ (grade); those two are the same party and count once. No further independent grading was found; the beta already states both figures.

No source gives a car-to-car gain for the West Face Wall routes; a Gorillas in the Mist search summary gives only a whole-day figure for a different Stuart outing. gain_ft 1663 is below the trailhead-to-wall rise, but writing a figure would mean computing it from pins, which is not allowed.

No source states the approach distance from the Esmeralda trailhead to the West Face Wall; dist_km 7.2 (4.5 mi) remains shorter than the row's own 7.5 mi summit waypoint, but no researched one-way figure exists to replace it.

results.fact: Commitment grade (commitment III vs beta 'Grade: IV')
results.evidence: commitment says III while the beta opens 'Grade: IV 5.11+'. The IV comes from the first-ascent party's journal note; the route database page gives no Grade numeral, and the neighbouring Gorillas in the Mist is listed as Grade IV, which is suggestive but is a different route. Only one source for this route, so no patch.
